intro: «Para» + infinitive when the purpose is your own; «para que» + subjunctive when another person must act.
p.para.consejo: With «para» + infinitive you state your own purpose: «estudio para aprender».
p.para que.consejo: Always with the subjunctive: «hablo despacio para que entiendas». If it is the same subject, use only «para».
p.aprender.consejo: It takes no «a» before a noun, but it does before a verb: «aprendo a nadar».
p.entender.consejo: It changes e to ie: «entiendo», «entiendas». In «entendemos» the e does not change.
p.a tiempo.consejo: It is a fixed expression: «llegar a tiempo». Do not mix it up with «a veces».
p.explicar.consejo: Before e, the c becomes «qu»: «explique», «expliques». That way it keeps the k sound.
p.ayudar.consejo: The y sounds as in «yo»: «a-yu-DAR». You say «ayudar a alguien con algo».
p.regalo.consejo: It is masculine: «el regalo». The verb is «regalar»: «te regalo un libro».
p.sorpresa.consejo: It is feminine: «una sorpresa». The verb is «sorprender».
p.objetivo.consejo: The j sounds h: «ob-he-TI-bo». It is also an adjective: «objetivo» = unbiased.
p.preparar.consejo: You can prepare a meal, a party or a trip. A gift you «buy».
b1.titulo: Your own purpose, or someone else's
b1.texto:
To say **what for** you do something, you have two ways:

- If the person acting is **the same**, use **para + infinitive**: Estudio **para aprender**.
- If **another person** must act, use **para que + subjunctive**: Te llamo **para que vengas**. Hablo despacio **para que entiendas**.

That is why you do not say «Te llamo para vengas» (missing **que**) or «Estudio para que aprendo» (the subject is the same).

The question is **¿para qué?** («what for?»). **¿Por qué?** asks about the cause.
b2.f0.texto: I am preparing a surprise for my sister.
b2.f1.texto: What do you need my help for?
b2.f2.texto: I am calling you so you can help me with the gift.
b2.f3.texto: I leave work early to arrive on time.
b2.f4.texto: I explain the plan slowly so that everyone understands it.
b2.f5.texto: I buy balloons to decorate the room.
b2.f6.texto: I hide the cake so that she does not see it.
b2.f7.texto: I keep quiet so that nobody spoils the surprise.
b4.texto:
Purpose answers the question **¿para qué?** (what for?)

- **Same subject** → **para + infinitive**: Salgo pronto **para llegar** a tiempo.
- **Different subject** → **para que + subjunctive**: Te explico el plan **para que lo entiendas**.

Other, slightly more formal purpose formulas: **a fin de que**, **con el objetivo de que**, **de modo que** + subjunctive.

Compare **para** and **por**: **para** looks forward (the goal); **por** looks back (the cause). Estudio **para** aprender. Estudio **por** curiosidad.
b4.e0.texto: I study every day in order to learn.
b4.e1.texto: I speak slowly so that you understand.
b4.e2.texto: I explain the plan to you so that you have no doubts.
b5.f0.texto: The room dresses up in yellow balloons and blue ribbons.
b5.f1.texto: A garland of lights hangs from wall to wall like a little sky.
b5.f2.texto: Lucía climbs onto a chair with a nail between her teeth.
b5.f3.texto: Pablo holds the ladder with both hands and looks upwards.
b5.f4.texto: The hammer strikes the wall with a dry echo.
b5.f5.texto: On the table rests a strawberry cake with a white candle.
b5.f6.texto: A gift wrapped in golden paper waits by the door.
b5.f7.texto: Outside you can hear light footsteps on the dry leaves.
b5.f8.texto: Everyone holds their breath behind the sofa.
b5.f9.texto: The door opens slowly and lets in a warm light.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! «Para que» always takes the subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The infinitive does not go after «para que».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Vienes» is indicative; here you need the subjunctive.
b6.pregunta: You want another person to come. What is missing?
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is for when another person acts.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Para que» does not take the indicative for purpose.
b7.pregunta: You study and you learn. What do you use?
b8.o0.refuerzo: «Entiendes» is indicative; the subjunctive is missing.
b8.o2.refuerzo: After «que» you need a conjugated verb.
b8.pregunta: You want your friend to understand you. What is missing?
b9.frase: Estudio todos los días para aprender
b9.traduccion: I study every day in order to learn
b10.o2.refuerzo: Yes! «Para qué» asks about the goal.
b10.pregunta: Which question asks for the purpose?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I call you so that you come».
b12.o0.refuerzo: That would be another person. Here it is you.
b12.pregunta: You yourself arrive. What is missing?
p.necesitas.consejo: From «necesitar», to need. The -as ending means «you».
p.explico.consejo: From «explicar», to explain. The «x» sounds like «ks».
p.entiendan.consejo: From «entender». With «para que» the subjunctive is used: «entiendan».
p.globos.consejo: Rubber bags filled with air for parties. The «g» before «o» is hard.
p.escondo.consejo: From «esconder», to hide. The ending -o means «I».
p.vea.consejo: After «para que», the subjunctive is used: «vea». The «v» sounds like «b».
p.callo.consejo: From «callar», to be silent. The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.arruine.consejo: From «arruinar», to ruin. The subjunctive appears after «para que».
p.estudio.consejo: From «estudiar». The «ia» ending in the verb is one syllable: «es-TU-dyo».
p.entiendas.consejo: From «entender». The subjunctive form ends in -as after a verb of wanting.
p.cintas.consejo: Long narrow strips of cloth. The «c» before «i» sounds like «th».
p.guirnalda.consejo: A chain of flowers or lights for decoration. It is feminine: «la guirnalda».
p.clavo.consejo: A thin metal piece hammered into walls. The «v» sounds like «b».
p.martillo.consejo: A tool used to hit nails. The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.oyen.consejo: From «oír», to hear. The «oy» here is one syllable: «O-yen».
p.ligeros.consejo: The «g» before «e» sounds like «h». It agrees with «pasos», so it is plural.
p.contienen.consejo: From «contener», to hold inside. The «ie» is one syllable: «kon-TYE-nen».
p.infinitivo.consejo: The basic verb form, like «hablar». The «v» sounds like «b».
